## Recommendation
- Fish the Grand Haven pier. It's the only one of the four with a recent pier rating above slow, but expect a slow-to-below-average bite.
- Expected pier ratings (0-4): Grand Haven 1, St. Joseph 0, South Haven 0 (no pier report, estimate), Muskegon 0 (no pier report, estimate).
- Cast glow spoons or glow plugs, and plan to be there in low light at dawn or dusk, when the pier catches have come in.
- If you want a better bet, the boat reports were stronger than the pier reports. Run J-plugs or meat rigs around 40-90 feet down, in 70-150 feet of water off Grand Haven.

## Why
- Grand Haven is the best pier bet because its last two pier reports were rated below average, while St. Joseph's was slow and Muskegon and South Haven had no pier report at all (Grand Haven, 2023-08-23 and 2023-08-30).
- Glow spoons and plugs are the lures pier anglers caught fish on, and the Grand Haven report said the spoon catches came in low light (Grand Haven, 2023-08-30; Grand Haven, 2023-08-23).
- I'd expect pier fishing to stay slow this week because the last three days showed no upwelling wind at any of the four ports, and the pier bite usually picks up when cold water is pushed toward shore (Michigan Sea Grant guidance; conditions lookup for the week before today).

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest is 2023-08-30, six days old)
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-30, pier: "Pier anglers caught a few salmon while casting spoons in low light conditions." Rated 1 (below average).
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-23, pier: "A few salmon were caught off the piers while casting glow spoons." Rated 1.
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-16, pier: "Pier anglers who were casting spoons found the freshwater drum and salmon bite to be slow. Glow spoons and plugs worked well." Rated 0.
- St. Joseph, 2023-08-30, pier: "Pier anglers who targeted trout and salmon had slow fishing." Rated 0. Wind gusted to 52 mph that week.
- St. Joseph, 2023-08-09, pier: a few coho on nightcrawlers, described as "a little on the slow side."
- South Haven and Muskegon: no pier reports in the last six weeks.
- Boats (for comparison): Grand Haven, 2023-08-30, rated 3, "Glow or chrome J-plugs worked well" at 40-80 feet of water. Muskegon, 2023-08-30, rated 0. South Haven, 2023-08-30, rated 0, with the best water around 90-120 feet.

**Past seasons** (similar water temperature, September; history only)
- In Septembers with similar water, pier reports were mostly slow: Grand Haven 2022-09-14 "The pier action was slow for salmon," Grand Haven 2022-09-07 "slow for salmon," and Muskegon 2022-09-07 "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls."
- Grand Haven 2022-09-21 is the one exception I found: pier anglers caught a few on glow spoons, rated 0.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions lookup returned a summary of the week before today, not live readings. It shows no upwelling wind in the last three days at any of the four ports.
- Satellite surface water near the piers in that summary was 67-71 °F and warming over the last three days at all four ports (St. Joseph +2, South Haven +3, Grand Haven +4, Muskegon +3). Those are satellite values, not buoy readings.
- The NOAA lake model for the pierheads was not available in that summary, so I couldn't check the pier cold-water layer.

## Caveats
- The newest report is six days old (2023-08-30), and fall conditions change quickly.
- The ratings for South Haven and Muskegon are my estimates from boat reports and past seasons, not pier reports.
- The conditions data came back as a backtest summary rather than live readings, so I couldn't confirm today's water or the wind forecast.
- Any pier bite this week depends on a north-to-east wind pushing cold water in, which I'd expect to pick up the pier bite. Check the forecast before you go.
